cat > forgemyspec-bundle/dir-organizer/spec.yaml <<'EOF'
version: "0.1"
title: Directory Organizer
objective: >-
  A single-file, stdlib-only Python program organizer.py that moves the files sitting directly in a target
  directory into subdirectories named after their extension, once (--once) or continuously (--watch),
  logging every move to organizer.log.
execution_mode: critical
context:
  system: >-
    Empty Python repository, macOS/Linux, Python 3 standard library only. Deliverable is ./organizer.py with
    unittest tests under ./tests.
  assumptions:
    - "The target directory is a positional argument; it defaults to the current directory."
    - "The subdirectory name is the lowercase extension without the dot (report.PDF goes to pdf/)."
    - "A file with no extension goes to a subdirectory named no_extension."
    - "Only the last suffix counts (archive.tar.gz goes to gz/)."
    - "organizer.log is written inside the target directory and is never moved; organizer.py is never moved either."
    - "If the destination already has a file with the same name, the moved file gets a numeric suffix (name_1.ext) and nothing is overwritten."
    - "Watch mode polls the directory every --interval seconds (default 2) and stops on Ctrl-C; no third-party watcher is used."
    - "Subdirectories are never descended into and never moved; only regular files at the top level are organized."
constraints:
  - "Single file organizer.py; Python standard library only, no third-party packages."
  - "Files inside subdirectories are not touched, and no recursion happens."
  - "Hidden files (names starting with a dot) are not moved."
  - "Existing files are never overwritten or deleted."
  - "No configuration file, no custom extension mapping, no GUI, no daemonization."
success_criteria:
  - "Running --once on a directory with mixed files leaves each top-level file in its extension subdirectory."
  - "Every move appends one line to organizer.log naming source and destination."
  - "--watch organizes files that appear after it starts."
  - "Hidden files and files already in subdirectories stay where they are."
hypotheses:
  - id: h1
    description: "--once moves each top-level regular file into a subdirectory named after its lowercase extension, then exits."
    confidence: 0.9
  - id: h2
    description: "--watch keeps running and organizes files that appear in the target directory after startup."
    confidence: 0.8
  - id: h3
    description: "Every move is appended to organizer.log with timestamp, source and destination."
    confidence: 0.9
  - id: h4
    description: "Hidden files and files already inside subdirectories are left untouched."
    confidence: 0.9
  - id: h5
    description: "organizer.py is one file that imports only the Python standard library."
    confidence: 0.9
  - id: h6
    description: "A name collision at the destination never overwrites an existing file."
    confidence: 0.85
required_evidence:
  - "Output of the unittest run in tests showing all boundary tests passing."
  - "Output of the gate command ending in RESULT: PASS."
actions:
  - id: a1
    description: "Implement file classification (skip rules, extension to subdirectory name) in organizer.py."
    type: implement
    requires_confirmation: false
    supports: [h1, h4]
  - id: a2
    description: "Implement the move with collision-safe naming and logging to organizer.log."
    type: implement
    requires_confirmation: false
    supports: [h3, h6]
  - id: a3
    description: "Implement the CLI with --once and --watch modes."
    type: implement
    requires_confirmation: false
    supports: [h1, h2]
  - id: a4
    description: "Write unittest tests for every obligation and check the stdlib-only import rule."
    type: test
    requires_confirmation: false
    supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6]
  - id: a5
    description: "Run the gate and review the report."
    type: validate
    requires_confirmation: false
    supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6]
decision_rules:
  - "If a behavior is not covered by an obligation, stop and request a spec amendment."
  - "If a test fails, fix organizer.py, never weaken the test."
metadata:
  source_prompt: >-
    Build a Directory Organizer in Python. Watch a target directory and move files into subdirectories by
    extension. Two modes: --watch and --once. Log moves to organizer.log. Skip files already in subdirs and
    hidden files. Single file organizer.py, stdlib only.
  generator: claude-code-session
  scope_contract:
    must_include:
      - "move files into subdirectories by extension"
      - "--once mode"
      - "--watch mode"
      - "log moves to organizer.log"
      - "skip files already in subdirs"
      - "skip hidden files"
      - "single file organizer.py"
      - "stdlib only"
formal:
  module: OrganizerCore
  obligations:
    - id: once_moves_by_extension
      kind: boundary
      statement: "--once moves each top-level regular file into a subdirectory named after its lowercase extension and exits 0."
      hypotheses: [h1]
      must_include: ["move files into subdirectories by extension", "--once mode"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizerTests.test_once_moves_by_extension"
    - id: watch_organizes_new_files
      kind: boundary
      statement: "--watch keeps running and moves a file created after startup into its extension subdirectory."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["--watch mode"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizerTests.test_watch_organizes_new_files"
    - id: moves_logged
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Each move appends a line with timestamp, source and destination to organizer.log in the target directory."
      hypotheses: [h3]
      must_include: ["log moves to organizer.log"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizerTests.test_moves_logged"
    - id: skips_files_in_subdirs
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Files already inside subdirectories are not moved and subdirectories are not descended into."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["skip files already in subdirs"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizerTests.test_skips_files_in_subdirs"
    - id: skips_hidden_files
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Files whose name starts with a dot are not moved."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["skip hidden files"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizerTests.test_skips_hidden_files"
    - id: single_file_stdlib_only
      kind: boundary
      statement: "organizer.py imports only standard library modules and needs no other project file."
      hypotheses: [h5]
      must_include: ["single file organizer.py", "stdlib only"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizerTests.test_single_file_stdlib_only"
    - id: collision_not_overwritten
      kind: boundary
      statement: "When the destination name exists, the moved file gets a numeric suffix and the existing file is unchanged."
      hypotheses: [h6]
      must_include: ["move files into subdirectories by extension"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizerTests.test_collision_not_overwritten"
scope:
  paths: ["organizer.py", "tests/**"]
  tests: tests
  pythonpath: ["."]
EOF
H=.forgemyspec/harness
PYTHONPATH=$H python3 -m forgemyspec lint forgemyspec-bundle/dir-organizer/spec.yaml --formal && PYTHONPATH=$H python3 -m forgemyspec package forgemyspec-bundle/dir-organizer/spec.yaml; PYTHONPATH=$H python3 -m forgemyspec board start R1; PYTHONPATH=$H python3 -m forgemyspec board

result:
The spec passes lint with 100/100 and no warnings. It's waiting for your approval before I write any code. The approval covers the spec in `forgemyspec-bundle/dir-organizer/spec.yaml`, which is a spec-only bundle. All 7 obligations are boundary tests, with no Dafny proofs.

**What you'd be approving**
- **Modes:** `--once` organizes the top-level files and exits. `--watch` polls the directory every `--interval` seconds (default 2) until Ctrl-C.
- **Destination:** each top-level regular file goes into a subdirectory named after its lowercase extension, so `report.PDF` goes to `pdf/`.
- **Skipped:** hidden files (names starting with a dot) and anything already inside a subdirectory. Subdirectories are never entered.
- **Log:** every move appends a line to `organizer.log` with a timestamp, the source and the destination.
- **Packaging:** everything is in a single `organizer.py`, standard library only.

**Assumptions I made. Say if any is wrong.**
- The target directory is a positional argument and defaults to the current directory.
- A file with no extension goes to `no_extension/`.
- Only the last suffix counts, so `archive.tar.gz` goes to `gz/`.
- `organizer.log` is written inside the target directory and is never moved. `organizer.py` is never moved either.
- If the destination already has a file with that name, the moved file gets a numeric suffix (`name_1.ext`). Nothing is overwritten.
- Watch mode polls rather than using a filesystem-events library, because only the standard library is allowed.

**To approve**, type this code in the chat: `UAJ23W`.
